singular_truth: oh-my-pi addresses every edit by the content hash of the surrounding code, not by a line number. It edits by what the code IS, not where it sits.
money_thing: an edit re-finding its exact target by content-hash after the file has shifted underneath, while a line-number edit silently lands in the wrong place and corrupts the file.
logline: Most coding agents paste edits at a line number and pray they land; oh-my-pi anchors every edit to the code's own content hash, so it lands on exactly the right place or it is rejected.
rejected_default: The obvious treatment for a terminal coding agent is a terminal typing `omp`, a node-diagram touring its 32 tools, a flash, and wordmark bookends. Rejected: that is a feature TOUR that shows WHAT it has and buries the ONE singular idea (content-hash editing) in a tool cloud. It never shows WHY the edit can't miss. The singular truth is a mechanism, so the video must dramatize the mechanism, not inventory the toolbox.
references: git's content-addressed objects (a blob keyed by its hash, not its path)
